title: The day the bread didn’t fall

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? when did you last have a whole day with no work in it at all?
options: then this story was made for you. listen.
good. let’s see where that idea began. listen.
then listen closely. this one is about permission.

steps.line: In the desert after Egypt, the freed slaves were hungry. “In Egypt, we ate bread until we were full,” they grumbled.
So each morning, when the dew lifted, the ground was covered with something fine and white, like frost. “What is it?” they asked. In Hebrew, man hu. Manna.
Everyone gathered what they needed for the day. Some gathered more, some less, and yet no one had too much, and no one had too little.

steps.q: You were a slave; you know hunger. You’re told not to keep any manna till morning. Some did anyway. What happened?
o: It was full of worms by morning
steps.why: Exodus 16:20: by morning it bred worms and stank, and Moses was angry. Saving up didn’t work; the bread came one day at a time.

steps.q: On the sixth morning, they go out to gather as usual. What do you guess is on the ground?
steps.why: Twice as much (Exodus 16:22), so the seventh could be a day of stopping. And this time it kept overnight without spoiling.

steps.line: On the sixth day, there was twice as much. Moses told them: tomorrow is a day of rest, a holy Shabbat. Bake what you need today.
On the seventh day, some went out anyway with their baskets. They found nothing. So the people rested on the seventh day.

steps.pre: The word Shabbat comes from a Hebrew root that means to
steps.why: Stop, shavat. Not ‘relax’ exactly: Shabbat is stopping work, even when there’s more you could do.

steps.line: Today, many Jewish families set two loaves of challah on the Shabbat table, under a cloth. Two loaves, for the double bread before that first rest.
steps.label: today

steps.q: The two loaves sit under a cloth. Why the cloth, many say?
o: Like the dew that covered the manna
To keep the bread warm for the blessing
So no one eats before the meal
steps.why: Dew lay below and above the manna, so the board and cloth echo it. Another lovely reason: so the bread isn’t ‘shamed’ while the wine is blessed first.

say: here’s what i love. the rest was prepared before anyone asked for it. the bread was doubled first, so nobody had to choose between eating and stopping.
later the torah gives a reason to rest: you were slaves once, so let your servants rest as well as you, even the stranger and the ox. in jewish tradition, rest isn’t a prize. it’s owed to everyone.

steps.q: On the seventh day, the manna itself stopped, not just the people. What does that suggest about Shabbat?
o: Rest is built into the world itself
Rest is for people who finished their work
Rest is up to each person to choose
steps.why: The world itself paused. Shabbat isn’t time you steal from work. It arrives on schedule, for everyone.

today.say: plan a little rest the way the manna did: do one chore today, so tomorrow has room to stop. and if someone works for you or with you, make sure they get a break as well as you.
options: double bread first, then a day to stop. that’s the gift.
i know. this day was made for people who couldn’t stop.
